resources.name: Central Texas Food Bank
resources.description: Get free groceries from many food pantries in Austin and nearby areas. They also help you apply for SNAP (food stamps) and other food help. Some pantries are drive‑through. Times and days are different by site. You can search by zip code on their website or call for help. No cost, but some sites may ask basic questions about your income and family size. Bring a photo ID if you have one. If you do not have ID, still call and ask. Staff can explain what papers you need.
resources.availability_status: Open - pantry and mobile food schedule varies by location and day

resources.name: Caritas of Austin
resources.description: Get free groceries and basic food items if you are low income or without housing. They run a food pantry and also give help with finding other food places. They mainly help people in Austin who are homeless or at high risk of losing housing. You may first meet with a helper who works with you. They can also help with benefits like SNAP (food stamps). Call first to learn pantry hours and what papers you need. Walk‑ins may be limited.
resources.availability_status: Open - call for current food pantry hours and any limits

resources.name: El Buen Samaritano
resources.description: Get free groceries from a drive‑through food pantry if you are low income. They serve people in Austin and Travis County. Food help is usually by set days and times each week. They may also help you apply for SNAP (food stamps) and other programs. You may need to give your name, address, and family size. No Social Security number is needed. Call or check the website for pantry schedule and what papers you need to bring.
resources.availability_status: Open - food pantry days and hours can change, call before you go

resources.name: SAFE Alliance - Food and Basic Needs for Clients
resources.description: Get free food, meals, and basic items if you are getting help for family or partner violence or sexual assault. Help is for people who are clients in SAFE housing or programs. They give meals in shelter and food boxes and gift cards when they can. They may also help you find other food places in Austin. Call the hotline to learn how to become a client and what help you can get. You do not need to pay for these services.
resources.availability_status: Open for current and new clients - call hotline first

resources.name: Meals on Wheels Central Texas
resources.description: Get free or low‑cost meals delivered to your home if you are an older adult or an adult with a disability. They serve people in Austin and nearby areas. Call to apply and learn who can get help.
resources.availability_status: Open - some routes may have a wait list, call to check

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul Society - Diocesan Council of Austin
resources.description: Get help with food, groceries, and basic needs if you are low income. Local church groups under St. Vincent de Paul may give food bags, gift cards, or help paying for food. resources.name: Texas Health and Human Services - SNAP (Food Stamps)
resources.description: Get monthly money for food through SNAP (food stamps) if your income is low. You can use a Lone Star Card like a debit card at most grocery stores. You need papers like ID, pay stubs, and a lease if you have one. If you need help with the form, call or visit an office.
resources.availability_status: Open - SNAP applications accepted year round

Staff can help you use your GI Bill and other veteran programs. They work closely with Texas Veterans Commission staff on‑site. Call or visit to sign up and ask about walk‑in times.
resources.address: 9001 N Interstate Hwy 35, Suite 110, Austin, TX 78753
resources.availability_status: Open – some services may require an appointment

resources.name: Easterseals Central Texas – Veteran and Military Services
resources.description: Get free support for veterans and families, like someone to talk to and help with goals. They help with stress, trauma, housing, money, and work plans. Staff can go with you to appointments and help you talk with other groups. They also help you find job training and school options. Call to see what help is open now.
resources.address: 8505 Cross Park Dr, Suite 120, Austin, TX 78754
resources.availability_status: Open – some programs may have a waitlist

resources.name: Heroes Night Out – Veteran Support Center
resources.description: Get peer support, social events, and help finding mental health and job help for veterans. This is a drop‑in center where veterans and families can meet other veterans. Staff and volunteers help connect you to doctors, someone to talk to, and job programs. Many events are free. Call or check online for hours and events.
resources.address: 1150 S Bell Blvd, Cedar Park, TX 78613
resources.availability_status: Open – call to confirm current hours
